name: Christchurch Botanic Gardens
bio: Twenty-one hectares of heritage trees, rose gardens and glasshouses wrapped in a loop of the Avon River.

name: Avon River / Ōtākaro
bio: Glide past willows and the Botanic Gardens in a flat-bottomed punt, poled by a boater in Edwardian dress.

name: Christchurch Art Gallery
bio: Te Puna o Waiwhetū, a striking glass-fronted gallery holding the region's finest New Zealand and international art.

name: The Arts Centre
bio: A Gothic Revival former university campus, restored after the earthquakes and home to galleries, cafés and markets.

name: Cardboard Cathedral
bio: Shigeru Ban's A-frame 'transitional' cathedral, built from giant cardboard tubes after the 2011 earthquake.

name: New Regent Street
bio: A pastel-painted 1930s Spanish Mission street of cafés and boutiques, with the heritage tram running down the middle.

name: Riverside Market
bio: A buzzing indoor market hall of food stalls, bakeries, bars and local produce on the banks of the Avon.

name: International Antarctic Centre
bio: Brave a polar storm room, ride an all-terrain Hägglund and meet rescued little blue penguins beside the airport.

name: Christchurch Gondola
bio: A cable car up the Port Hills to views over the city, Lyttelton Harbour, the Canterbury Plains and the Alps.

name: Lyttelton
bio: A steep-streeted harbour town in an extinct volcano's caldera, with bars on London Street and the Timeball Station.

name: Lyttelton Timeball Station
bio: A time-signal tower of 1876 whose ball dropped daily at 1 PM, destroyed in the 2011 earthquake and rebuilt in 2017–18.

name: Sumner Beach
bio: The sandy beach of the seaside suburb of Sumner, with Cave Rock at its end and the Port Hills rising behind.

name: Godley Head
bio: A headland at the mouth of Lyttelton Harbour with a WWII gun battery and a three-hour loop walk from Taylors Mistake.

name: Bridle Path
bio: A steep track of about 1.5 hours one way from Heathcote over the Port Hills to Lyttelton, the route early settlers walked.

name: Corsair Bay
bio: A sandy swimming beach at the bottom of a steep-sided cove, one bay west of Lyttelton's port.

name: Ōtamahua / Quail Island
bio: An 81 ha uninhabited island in Lyttelton Harbour with safe swimming beaches, reached by ferry.

name: Hagley Park
bio: Christchurch's largest urban open space: 165 hectares of lawns and tree-lined paths beside the Botanic Gardens.

name: Canterbury Earthquake National Memorial
bio: The Crown's national memorial, a wall beside the Avon River, to those killed or seriously injured in the 22 February 2011 earthquake.

name: New Brighton Pier
bio: A concrete pier opened in 1997, one of the icons of Christchurch, jutting into the sea from New Brighton beach.

name: Orana Wildlife Park
bio: New Zealand's only open-range zoo, with endangered animals from around the world and a Lion Encounter.

name: Riccarton House and Bush
bio: The last forest remnant on the Canterbury Plains, set in the city beside the historic Riccarton House.

name: Ferrymead Heritage Park
bio: A recreated Edwardian township and museum with a horse and carriage, trams and trains on operating days.

name: Air Force Museum of New Zealand
bio: A museum of New Zealand military aviation at Wigram, beside the former RNZAF base, with full-size replica fighters.

name: Christchurch Adventure Park
bio: A Port Hills park of downhill and beginner mountain-bike trails with zip-lines and a chairlift.

name: Akaroa Harbour
bio: A flooded volcanic crater where cruises spot — and small groups swim with — rare Hector's dolphins beneath towering cliffs.

name: The Giant's House
bio: An 1880 house whose terraced gardens burst with sparkling mosaic sculptures by artist Josie Martin.

name: Akaroa Lighthouse
bio: A white timber lighthouse, moved from the harbour heads to the waterfront and now the emblem of the village.

name: Akaroa Museum
bio: Small but rich in stories of the peninsula's Ngāi Tahu, French and British settlers, including an 1858 courthouse.

name: Akaroa Head
bio: A clifftop reserve at the mouth of Akaroa Harbour, with old lighthouse-keeper house sites and Hector's dolphins offshore.

name: Banks Peninsula Track
bio: A private 31 km walk from Ōnuku through Flea Bay and Stony Bay, done over two or three days with huts, October to April.

name: Hinewai Reserve
bio: A private reserve of regenerating native forest east of Akaroa, with over 20 walking tracks free to enter on foot.

name: Okains Bay Museum
bio: A museum of Māori taonga, historic canoes and relocated colonial buildings in Okains Bay, 25 minutes from Akaroa.

name: Whale Watch Kaikōura
bio: Māori-owned boat trips over the Kaikōura Canyon to see giant sperm whales surface, blow and dive.

name: Kaikōura Peninsula Walkway
bio: A clifftop and shoreline loop past fur seal haul-outs, with the Seaward Kaikōura Range behind.

name: Ohau Point
bio: A roadside lookout over a large New Zealand fur seal colony, with pups playing in the rock pools in summer.

name: Fyffe House
bio: Kaikōura's oldest surviving building, an 1840s whaling cottage built on foundations of whale bone.

name: Mount Fyffe
bio: A long, steep climb to a 1,602 m summit with views along the coast and out over the Pacific.

name: Te Ana – The Caves
bio: A 91 m limestone sea cave beside State Highway 1, full of stalactites and stalagmites, reopened in late 2025.

name: Kaikōura Museum
bio: A town museum on the 2016 earthquake and the area's natural and social history, in a building shaped like a crayfish pot.

name: Point Kean
bio: The tip of the Kaikōura Peninsula, where fur seals bask a short walk from the car park and the Peninsula Walkway starts.

name: Nin's Bin
bio: A blue-and-white caravan on State Highway 1 at Half Moon Bay selling crayfish and fish and chips since 1977.

name: Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools
bio: Open-air rock pools, sulphur pools and waterslides fed by natural thermal springs beneath the mountains.

name: Conical Hill
bio: A short zigzag climb through forest to a lookout over the village and the Hanmer Basin.

name: Waiau Ferry Bridge
bio: A historic bridge over the Waiau Gorge, base for bungy jumps and jet-boat rides through the canyon.

name: TranzAlpine
bio: One of the world's great train journeys, crossing the Canterbury Plains and Southern Alps from Christchurch to Greymouth.

name: Avalanche Peak
bio: A steep, rewarding climb from the village to a summit facing glaciers on Mount Rolleston — kea are often for company.

name: Devils Punchbowl Falls
bio: A short walk through beech forest to a 131 m waterfall plunging off the valley wall.

name: Church of the Good Shepherd
bio: A little 1935 stone church on the lakeshore whose altar window frames the turquoise water and mountains.

name: Mount John University Observatory
bio: New Zealand's premier observatory, on a summit with 360° views over the Mackenzie Basin by day.

name: Dark Sky Project
bio: The Dark Sky Project's lakefront centre, where night-sky tours leave for Mount John and a daytime exhibit explains the reserve.

name: Tekapo Springs
bio: Hot pools with mountain views, plus winter ice skating and snow tubing at the foot of Mount John.

name: Sheepdog Statue
bio: A bronze collie beside the Church of the Good Shepherd, honouring the sheepdogs high-country farming depends on.

name: Hooker Valley Track
bio: An easy, spectacular walk over three swing bridges to an iceberg-dotted lake at the foot of Aoraki / Mount Cook.

name: Tasman Glacier
bio: New Zealand's longest glacier, viewed over its terminal lake from a short climb, or up close by boat among icebergs.

name: Mueller Hut
bio: A tough climb up the Sealy Tarns steps to an alpine hut facing hanging glaciers and the summit of Aoraki.

name: Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre
bio: A museum and planetarium at The Hermitage celebrating Hillary's life and the region's climbing history.

name: Lake Pukaki
bio: A vast glacial lake of startling blue, with Aoraki / Mount Cook rising at the head of the valley.

name: Kea Point
bio: A gentle walk from the village to a deck over the Mueller Glacier lake, Mount Sefton and Aoraki / Mount Cook.

name: Sealy Tarns
bio: About 2,200 steps, the stairway to heaven, climb to alpine tarns with views over the Hooker Valley and Aoraki.

name: Red Tarns
bio: A steep two-hour return climb from the village to tarns tinted red by pond weed, with views of Aoraki / Mount Cook.

name: Caroline Bay
bio: A sandy city beach with a summer carnival tradition, close to the town centre.

name: South Canterbury Museum
bio: A regional museum with natural history and the story of Richard Pearse's early flight experiments.

name: Te Ana Māori Rock Art Centre
bio: An interpretive centre on the Māori rock art of South Canterbury, with guided tours of the art in the region.

name: Aigantighe Art Gallery
bio: A regional art gallery in a historic house, set in sculpture-dotted gardens.

name: Kura Tāwhiti / Castle Hill
bio: Kura Tāwhiti, a surreal field of giant limestone boulders on a tussock hillside, sacred to Ngāi Tahu.

name: Cave Stream Scenic Reserve
bio: Wade 594 m through a dark limestone cave with a stream running through it — bring a torch and warm clothes.

name: Lewis Pass
bio: A 907 m pass on State Highway 7 through native beech forest, with a short nature walk around a tarn.

name: Birdlings Flat
bio: A pebble beach at the eastern end of Kaitorete Spit, well known for small agates, with Hector's dolphins offshore.
